`Does curl's --retry-all-errors option retry on HTTP error status codes without --fail?`

💡 Result:

No, curl's --retry-all-errors option does not cause curl to retry on HTTP error status codes (such as 4xx or 5xx) if the --fail option is not used [1][2]. By default, curl does not treat HTTP error status codes as "transfer errors" [1][2]. It considers a transfer to be successful as long as the HTTP response is fully received, even if the status code indicates an error (e.g., a 404 Not Found) [1]. The --retry-all-errors option expands the criteria for what constitutes a "transfer error" that triggers a retry, but it does not change the fundamental behavior that HTTP status codes are not considered failures [1][2]. To treat these HTTP error status codes as failures that trigger retries, you must use --fail (or --fail-with-body) in combination with --retry and --retry-all-errors [1][2][3].

Citations:

---
name: release-plz-workflow-compiles-needs-system-deps
description: release-plz.yml compiles the workspace (cargo publish --verify) — new system build deps (protoc etc.) must be added there too, not just ci.yml/msrv.yml
metadata:
  type: project
---

`release-plz.yml`'s `command: release` step runs `cargo publish --verify`, which **compiles every publishing crate's tarball on the runner**. Any new system-level build dependency must be installed in that workflow as well as the obvious CI ones.

**Why:** SMA-332 added the temporalio-* stack (`temporalio-protos` → `prost-wkt-types` build.rs needs system `protoc`, no vendored fallback). The protoc rollout covered ci.yml (clippy/test/docs/doc-coverage/build-no-default-features/sessions-it) + msrv.yml but missed release-plz.yml. Result (2026-07-06): the post-merge release published 3 of 5 crates in dependency order (core, mcp, agentcore), then failed verifying `runtime-temporal`'s tarball — a partial release. Registry stayed consistent (dependency-ordered publish means nothing published referenced the missing versions); hotfix PR #137 added the setup-protoc step and the re-triggered run published the rest (release-plz skips already-published versions — safe to re-run after partial releases).

**How to apply:** when adding any system build dependency, enumerate compiling workflows as: ci.yml jobs + msrv.yml + **release-plz.yml** (+ any future workflow running cargo build/test/doc/publish). A partial release from a verify failure is recoverable by fixing the workflow and pushing to main — do not manually publish the stragglers.

Related: [[release-ascend-needs-core-bump]]

---
name: parallel-bg-sessions-share-main-checkout
description: Parallel background pipeline sessions share the main checkout and switch branches under each other — isolate into a git worktree the moment a foreign checkout appears
metadata:
  type: project
---

Sven runs multiple background feature-pipeline sessions concurrently against the same repo. They all start in the main checkout, and each pipeline checks out its own `feature/sma-*` branch there — so a second session yanks the working tree out from under the first mid-run (observed 2026-07-05: an SMA-333 session checked out its branch while the SMA-332 session was between commits; also cargo-lock contention on `target/`).

**Why:** the background-session default is "work in place"; that assumption breaks silently the moment a sibling session starts.

**How to apply:** on detecting a foreign branch checkout in the shared tree (reflog shows a checkout you didn't make), don't fight over HEAD — `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<name> <your-branch>` + `EnterWorktree path:...` and continue there. During post-merge cleanup in this situation: fast-forward local main with `git fetch origin main:main` (no checkout), remove only your own worktree/branch, and never move the main checkout's HEAD — the sibling session owns it. Consider starting pipeline runs in a worktree from the outset when parallel sessions are likely.

# SMA-332 complete — all five crates published, everything cleaned up

**Release verified on crates.io:**

| Crate | Version | |
|---|---|---|
| `paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal` | **0.1.0** | first real release — durable Temporal runner |
| `paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore` | **0.1.0** | first real release — AgentCore shim |
| `paigasus-helikon-core` | 0.5.13 | additive durable-runner APIs |
| `paigasus-helikon-mcp` | 0.1.13 | stateless streamable-HTTP config |
| `paigasus-helikon` (facade) | 0.4.17 | both runtime features now resolve real crates |

The re-triggered release-plz run succeeded with the protoc fix, tags are pushed, no release PR is pending (nothing left to bump), and the book deployed. Only `paigasus-helikon-evals` remains a stub in the workspace.

**Cleanup:** both worktrees removed, both feature branches deleted, refs pruned, local `main` at `be0da80` — all without ever touching the main checkout's HEAD, which the SMA-333 session still owns. Linear closed SMA-332 on merge.

**Saved to memory** for future sessions: (1) `release-plz.yml` compiles the workspace during publish-verify, so system build deps like protoc must cover it too — the exact gap behind today's partial release; (2) parallel background sessions share the main checkout — isolate into a worktree the moment a foreign branch checkout appears.

**Still worth filing in Linear** (deliberate v0 gaps, all documented in code/spec): worker-side permission/redaction config + serializable-Ctx seed; `run_json` disconnect-finalize; `temporal-it` + Docker-build CI jobs; live workflow streaming / payload claim-check; A2A + AG-UI shims; `setup-protoc` version pin. Say the word and I'll create those tickets — otherwise the pipeline is done.
create the tickets
Creating the seven follow-up tickets in Linear, all linked to SMA-332:

input.title: runtime-temporal: worker-side permission/redaction configuration + serializable-Ctx seed
input.description:
## Background

SMA-332 shipped the durable runner with **fixed safe defaults** on the worker: activities build `RunContext::ephemeral(ctx)` — redaction on (env-sourced secrets only), built-in destructive-effect guards on, no custom deny/allow rules, no permission policy, no approval handler, no `extra_secrets`. The approved spec (§5.8, see the as-built note in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-runtime-temporal-agentcore-design.md`) originally promised an *optional worker-side permission/redaction configuration*; v0 deliberately dropped it (final whole-branch review, Important #1) and the crate docs state the fixed defaults.

## Scope

* `TemporalAgentWorkerBuilder` knobs for worker-side posture: permission mode, deny/allow rules, permission policy, approval handler, `extra_secrets` / redaction settings — applied to the `RunContext` the activities fabricate (`activities.rs::TypedRuntime::run_context`).
* A serializable-`Ctx`-seed mechanism so request-scoped caller context can (optionally, explicitly) cross the client→worker boundary.
* Consider heartbeat-aware activities while in this area: `record_heartbeat` in `call_model`/`invoke_tool` would speed up server-side reclamation of abandoned attempts (CodeRabbit round-1 finding on PR #136, deferred as non-correctness — workflow-level cooperative cancel is already live-validated).

## Notes

Docs to update alongside: `runtime-temporal/src/lib.rs` "Worker-Side Posture and Security Boundary" section, README, spec §5.8 as-built note.

input.title: runtime-agentcore + runtime-axum: finalize one-shot JSON runs on client disconnect
input.description:
## Background

SMA-332's review fixed the SSE path in `runtime-agentcore` (detached driver + `DropGuard`: disconnect cancels the run, session still finalizes — `invoke.rs::run_sse`). The analogous gap remains in the **buffered JSON mode**: `run_json` awaits `runner.run(...)` inside the handler future, so a client disconnect drops the future and `TokioRunner::run`'s internal finalize never executes — the turn's session write is silently lost. `runtime-axum`'s one-shot path has the same class of gap (its streaming path uses `spawn_writer`, its one-shot may not — verify).

## Scope

* Either detach the JSON-mode run (same decoupled-driver pattern as SSE, result awaited over a channel) or explicitly document the accepted semantics in `run_json`'s docs.
* Audit `runtime-axum`'s one-shot handler for the same class and align both crates.
* Regression test: JSON-mode client disconnect mid-run → session snapshot still gains the turn (mirror the SSE disconnect test in `invoke.rs`).

Origin: PR #136 Task-13 re-review Minor (pre-existing class, out of that fix's scope).

content.text: SMA-455 and SMA-456 created. Continuing with the remaining five:

input.title: ci: add temporal-it and agentcore docker-build jobs
input.description:
## Background

SMA-332 shipped both validation suites as local-only by GATE 1 decision: the Temporal integration tests (`crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/tests/temporal_live.rs`, incl. the crash-resume AC) are env-gated on `TEMPORAL_TEST_SERVER` and loud-skip in CI; the AgentCore image checks (`scripts/agentcore-image-check.sh`, size + cold-start gates) run via runbook (`docs/runbooks/agentcore-image-check.md`).

## Scope

* **temporal-it job** (pattern: `sessions-it`): install the `temporal` CLI on the runner, `temporal server start-dev --headless`, run the suite with `TEMPORAL_TEST_SERVER=localhost:7233 -- --test-threads=1`. Path-filtered to the temporal crate + core. Signal-only first; promote to required after it proves stable (the crash-resume test is wall-clock-sensitive — see the generous backstops in the suite).
* **agentcore docker-build job**: build both images (echo + `--features example-anthropic` agent) on an arm64 runner (or buildx+qemu), run the four gates from `scripts/agentcore-image-check.sh`. Signal-only.
* Remember the SMA-332 lesson: any job compiling the workspace needs the `setup-protoc` step.

input.title: ci: pin an explicit protoc version in setup-protoc steps
input.description:
## Background

SMA-332 added `arduino/setup-protoc` (SHA-pinned, v3.0.0) to every compiling workflow (ci.yml ×6 jobs, msrv.yml, release-plz.yml after PR #137), but without a `version:` input — the action defaults to the latest protoc release, so a future protoc release could break CI days later, unpinned and unrelated to any repo change. Flagged in the Task-4 review of PR #136 as a supply-chain-consistency Minor (the rest of the repo pins SHAs/digests everywhere).

## Scope

One-line `version:` input on every `setup-protoc` step (choose the current stable major, e.g. `version: "31.x"` per the action's syntax), then let Dependabot's github-actions group track the action itself. Single `chore(workflows)` or `ci(workflows)` commit; remember release-infra commit-type rules (never feat/fix).

input.title: runtime-temporal: live event streaming from the workflow
input.description:
## Background

SMA-332's `TemporalRunner::run_streamed` is **buffered, not live** (documented): it awaits workflow completion, then replays the recorded `AgentEvent`s as an immediate stream. Persistence is stronger than the trait contract (events are finalized before the stream exists), but consumers get no incremental progress during a durable run.

## Scope

* Live event delivery from the in-flight workflow — candidate mechanisms: Temporal queries polled by the runner, workflow updates, or an activity-side event sink the client tails. Evaluate against the Rust SDK's current (0.5+) support surface.
* Preserve the existing semantics: buffered fallback, `RunResultStreaming::with_failure` wiring, terminal-wins precedence.
* Raw token deltas still never cross the activity boundary (semantic events only) unless the design revisits that explicitly (payload-budget implications — see the crate docs' budget section).

input.title: runtime-temporal: payload claim-check offloading + compaction integration
input.description:
## Background

The durable runner's v0 envelope is bounded by Temporal payload limits: every `call_model` activity input carries the full conversation-so-far (O(N²) history growth), practical ceiling ~1.5 MB of conversation JSON (~15–20 turns at ≤50 KB tool outputs); a single oversized tool result fails its activity. Documented with arithmetic in `runtime-temporal`'s crate docs (SMA-332, spec §5.11).

## Scope

* Temporal payload codec / claim-check pattern: offload large payloads to blob storage, pass references through history.
* Compaction integration: drive `CompactingSession` / `LoopState::Compacting` from the durable driver so long conversations shrink instead of growing quadratically (coordinates with core's compaction support — `Compacting` is not driveable in core yet either).
* Revisit the documented envelope + escape hatches once either lands.

input.title: runtime-agentcore: A2A and AG-UI protocol shims
input.description:
## Background

SMA-332 shipped the HTTP (8080 `/invocations` + `/ping`) and MCP (8000 `/mcp`) protocol modes. AWS Bedrock AgentCore also supports two further GA protocols the crate doesn't cover (verified against AWS docs, July 2026):

* **A2A** — port 9000, mount path `/` (root), JSON-RPC 2.0 + agent-card discovery (GA since the Oct 2025 AgentCore launch).
* **AG-UI** — port 8080, `/invocations` (SSE) + `/ws` (added ~March 2026).

The optional WebSocket `GET /ws` endpoint on the HTTP protocol (64 KB frames, 250 fps) is also unimplemented.

## Scope

* `serve_a2a()` / AG-UI mode on `AgentCoreServer`, mirroring the existing builder + contract-test approach (`Router::oneshot` contract tests, README contract tables, book page section).
* Contract sources: AWS runtime protocol-contract pages (see the crate README's links and the SMA-332 spec §2 research notes).
